content: During the COVID-19 pandemic, there has been a significant rise in the incidence of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), particularly among children with type 1 diabetes. This increase is largely attributed to delays in diagnosis and medical intervention caused by disruptions in healthcare systems. These delays have resulted in more frequent and severe presentations of DKA. Research conducted during the early phases of the pandemic has underscored the heightened risk of DKA in individuals newly diagnosed with diabetes. This is likely due to restricted access to healthcare services and delays in recognizing and addressing the symptoms of diabetes in a timely manner.
